persona: SUB-01: a 20-year-old university student who lives alone in a small apartment in Kichijoji, Tokyo. Part-time job on weekend shifts. An ordinary young adult, not special.

time.scale: 24x: one real hour is one simulated day, so one simulated hour is 2.5 real minutes
time.after_midnight: 24:00 or later is after midnight of the same template day (25:00 is 01:00)
time.durations: simulated minutes as [min, max], drawn uniformly as life.py draws its ACTIVITIES ranges

weekly_rules.weekend_shifts: one or two: the Saturday shift always happens (weight 1.0), the Sunday shift half the time (weight 0.5)
weekly_rules.weekly_chores: laundry and cleaning once a week, both on Sunday

leisure.draw: drawn again and again to fill free time; only entries whose window contains the current time take part, weights renormalised among them

notes: Reading of the brief: teeth are daily (weight 1.0) and the shower is daily at 0.9; laundry and cleaning are once a week, both on Sunday; dishes come after 70% of days. Travel to campus, the library and the job is not modelled, so a consumer keeps him away for the whole block plus travel.

The hint (daily_plan.hint) reads the shared part only: a typical weekday at home. Entries in day_types are for a consumer that knows the weekday. Each entry takes part from earliest_start to latest_start; a sleep entry from target_start to wake.target (the whole night). The highest weight wins, ties go to the earlier entry, null activities are ignored, and a meal step has its option's weight.

Sleep: onset 00:30 is sleep.py's usual onset (next_bedtime). The wake target 08:00 is sleep.py's alarm (ALARM_HOUR 8, or SUB01_WAKE_HOUR), so the template and the engine agree; the brief's 8 to 9 is the wake window. Friday and Saturday nights (day_types.weekend) are later: onset 01:15, wake 09:30. sleep.py has no weekend alarm yet.
P1 shower: proposed activity 'shower', place 'bathroom' (new, see P11), 10-15 simulated min, need hygiene, after the 08:00 wake.
P2 teeth: proposed activity 'brush_teeth', place 'bathroom', 3-5 min, need hygiene; morning and night.
P3 class blocks: proposed activity 'attend_class', away at 'campus' (new, no route), 90 min per block, two per class day, need obligation.
P4 after-meal chore: proposed activity 'dishes', place 'kitchen' (new, see P11), 10-15 min, need chores, weight 0.7, after the evening meal.
P5 home cooking: proposed activity 'cook', place 'kitchen', 10-15 min, need hunger, before each home-cooked meal. Instant noodles count as home cooking.
P6 part-time job: proposed activity 'work_shift', away at 'job' (new, see P11), 300 min, need obligation. Saturday always, Sunday half the time, and 40% of non-class weekdays.
P7 library study: proposed activity 'library_study', away at 'library' (new, see P11), 90-120 min, need obligation; the other 60% of non-class weekdays.
P8 cleaning: proposed activity 'clean_apartment', once a week on Sunday, 30-45 min, need chores; the place is a point inside the apartment, to be chosen.
P9 laundry: proposed activity 'laundry', once a week on Sunday, 60-90 min, need hygiene; place bathroom or a washer point.
P10 needs not in life.py: hygiene, chores, obligation and curiosity (life.py's research why-text says 'curious'). life.py uses hunger and boredom; energy appears only in its module docstring.
P11 places not in life.py PLACES: bathroom, kitchen, campus, job and library. Away places need no point in the world; a consumer only keeps him off the apartment.
P12 konbini while the bakery is open: bf_konbini_buy and ln_konbini_buy (see G1). Null until life.py may buy_konbini in the bakery's hours; their eat steps stay.

G1 konbini: life.py scores buy_konbini only while the bakery is closed (about 19:58 to 06:58), with no food in stock and no delivery on its way. The dinner konbini option (20:00) fits as it is; the breakfast and lunch options need P12.

G2 ramen: life.py opens order_food from 10:00, only with hunger 0.55 or more, only with no food in stock and no delivery on its way, and at most once every 3 simulated hours. The courier arrives on its own, so get_delivery windows are targets. No ramen at breakfast.

G3 park: life.py opens the park at 08:00 on weekdays and 07:00 on weekends, and he must leave by 20:00. home-park is 1275 m (about 5 simulated min each way) and home-bakery 456 m (about 2 min), from web/tokyo_routes.json and life.py WALK_S.
G4 home devices: life.py scores play_console, use_computer and use_bathroom only when home_enabled is set. play_console offers pong, and Minecraft when configured.
G5 chat: life.py scores chat only while viewer messages wait (chat_waiting), so the chat window is a cap, not a guarantee.

G6 day counts: life.py counts meals and research per day from 04:00 (DAY_RESET_H) and weights research past 3 sessions a day to a quarter. This template uses calendar days, so a consumer must map the counts.
G7 not scheduled: watch_video, play_chess (one game a day in life.py), window and use_bathroom (bladder need). Sleep stages come from the sleep engine; the sleep times here are targets.
G8 bread: buy_bread here is a daily chance. life.py triggers bakery trips from bread stock (4 rolls a trip, 2 a meal), so a consumer should check stock before a bread option.
G9 meal windows: life.py meal slots are 07-10, 12-14 and 18-21. Preparation steps may start before a slot (lunch 11:30) so that eating starts inside it.

G10 bread and delivery: a delivery takes about 25 simulated minutes from the order to eating (order 2-4, cook 8-15, a ride of about 4 on the 927 m shop-home route), and life.py orders only at hunger 0.55 or more with no bread. While the bakery is open a bakery trip is faster, so each ramen option is 10% (was 25%) and errand_bread_dinner (17:30-18:15) keeps bread for the evening; without it he runs out of bread after the afternoon meal, and the late meal is a delivery (test_life_day, twelve days).
Risk: null activities cannot run in life.py until their proposals are approved and named, and hint() ignores them. The konbini and kitchen decisions (G1, P11, P12) are the owner's to make.
